name: Accessibility Issue
about: Report an accessibility barrier
labels: a11y

<!--
  Beginner? Start here.

  An accessibility issue means something in the project is harder to use (or
  impossible to use) for people with disabilities. You don't need to know WCAG
  numbers or technical details -- just describe what's hard and we'll classify it
  together. Every report helps.
-->

## Severity

- [ ] **Severe**: Blocks a complete task for assistive technology users
- [ ] **Moderate**: Workaround exists but experience is degraded
- [ ] **Minor**: Cosmetic or non-blocking issue

## What's the barrier

[Describe what you can't do or what's harder than it should be.]

## Who it affects

- [ ] Screen reader users
- [ ] Keyboard-only users
- [ ] Voice Control users
- [ ] Users with low vision / high contrast needs
- [ ] Users with motor impairments
- [ ] Users with cognitive disabilities
- [ ] Mobile / touch users
- [ ] Other: ___

## WCAG criterion (if known)

[e.g., 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value]

Common criteria for reference:
- **1.1.1** Non-text Content (images need alt text)
- **1.4.3** Contrast (Minimum) (color contrast)
- **2.1.1** Keyboard (keyboard access)
- **3.1.2** Language of Parts (lang attributes on non-English content)
- **4.1.2** Name, Role, Value (element names and roles)

1. [Step 1]
2. [Step 2]
3. [Step 3]

[What should happen for the user.]

## Actual behavior

[What happens instead.]

- OS: [e.g., Windows 11, macOS 14]

## Scope guard

- Allowed files: [files that should change to fix this]
- Out-of-scope files: [files that should NOT be touched]

## AI usage level

- [ ] **AIL-0**: No AI tools used
- [ ] **AIL-1**: AI-assisted (human wrote the core logic; AI helped with boilerplate, lookups, or suggestions)
- [ ] **AIL-2**: AI-generated (AI produced the primary output; human reviewed and edited)
